+# Entire Graph README A+ Plan
+
+Status: Draft for editing
+
+## Objective
+
+Turn the root README into a concise, credible landing page that lets a reader:
+
+1. Understand what Entire Graph is and is not.
+2. Install the prerequisite Entire CLI and the Entire Graph plugin.
+3. Activate Entire Graph for a coding agent with explicit repository side effects.
+4. Ask the agent a repository-source-read-only code question and verify that it
+   used graph evidence before inspecting focused source.
+5. Understand cache reuse and freshness, limits, data flow, and side effects.
+6. Reach detailed documentation without searching through the repository.
+
+This is a documentation-only project. It does not change CLI behavior, graph
+semantics, benchmarks, releases, the plugin catalog, or integrations.
+
+## Fixed assumptions
+
+- Keep the root filename exactly `README.md`.
+- At publication time, the official plugin index contains `graph` and a clean
+  `entire plugin install graph` succeeds on every platform the README claims.
+- Entire CLI 0.10.0 or later is already available through its documented
+  installation channels.
+- Setup uses the console, but day-to-day code discovery and analysis happen
+  through the coding agent in response to repository tasks.
+- Direct CLI use remains available for debugging, automation, and downstream tools;
+  it is not the primary user journey.
+
+## Open decisions
+
+- Which coding-agent clients have a tested instruction-loading and verification
+  path that the root README may name?
+- Which clean consuming fixture and pinned commit will produce the checked agent
+  transcript?
+- Which platforms will the installation example explicitly claim to support?
+- Is any quantitative result relevant enough for the root README? Default to none
+  unless one survives the claim audit.
+
+## Guiding principles
+
+- Make the recommended usage journey agent-first: setup installs and activates
+  Entire Graph, then the coding agent performs graph queries during repository work.
+- Disclose repository writes before asking the user to run `init-agents`, then
+  demonstrate the workflow with a repository-source-read-only task.
+- Prefer real commands, output, limits, and failure modes over adjectives.
+- Keep one canonical home for each substantial topic.
+- Scope every claim precisely; avoid absolutes such as “every,” “always,” and “zero” unless the contract proves them.
+- Keep benchmark evidence visible but move methodology and historical corrections out of the landing page.
+- Judge README length by usefulness, not an arbitrary line count.
+- Preserve existing URLs where practical; use compatibility pointers when documents move.
+
+## Competitor-informed requirements
+
+The comparison with [Graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/7fe58b0b0f3873be9a21c30106b8b8527c353aa6/README.md),
+[codebase-memory-mcp](https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/blob/d150ebe4fc78a9a3f85013d2087a849e5d59eb0f/README.md),
+[Mem0](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/96d45b78c702b742fc91a2ce9eae91805be9144b/README.md),
+[Graphiti](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/b2ff2eadd9a6b75a261a5cf0b19557883a13f752/README.md), and
+[Supermemory](https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/blob/82dae50ef458139823b3bfd3ebaaaac90ffd8a7c/README.md)
+produces four requirements:
+
+- Make a natural-language task—not a graph command—the first useful action.
+- Show observable agent events, focused source evidence, and the resulting answer;
+  never end the quickstart at “installed” or “done.”
+- Separate installation, instruction loading, graph adoption, and answer grounding
+  so users can verify each layer independently.
+- Keep reference material out of the landing page and label direct console use as
+  manual, diagnostic, or automation-oriented.
+
+## Target root README structure
+
+### 1. Hero and primary action
+
+- One short category sentence, for example: "Entire Graph is a local
+  static-analysis plugin that helps coding agents find definitions,
+  relationships, and change impact in Git repositories."
+- One supporting line can name tree-sitter and the main evidence types without
+  forcing every capability and audience into the opening sentence.
+- State the built-in analyzer’s no-egress boundary without implying that
+  installation itself is offline.
+- Make the primary journey explicit: install → activate for an agent → ask a
+  code question → inspect the evidence.
+- Link directly to installation, the first agent task, manual CLI use,
+  documentation, and limitations.
+- Avoid badge walls, slogans, release announcements, and unsupported superlatives.
+
+### 2. Prerequisites and installation
+
+- State that Entire Graph is an external command for the Entire CLI and that
+  `entire` 0.10.0 or later must already be installed and on `PATH`. Version
+  0.10.0 is the first stable Entire CLI release with remote name/URL plugin
+  installation.
+- Show the common macOS/Linux Entire CLI installation before the Entire Graph
+  installation:
+
+  ```sh
+  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
+  entire version
+  ```
+
+- Link other platforms and installation methods to the current
+  [Entire CLI installation documentation](https://docs.entire.io/installation)
+  instead of copying every platform command into this README.
+- Do not require `entire enable`; it configures Entire session capture and is
+  separate from dispatching the `entire graph` external command.
+- Install the indexed plugin and verify command dispatch:
+
+  ```sh
+  entire plugin install graph
+  entire graph version
+  ```
+
+  The install argument is `graph`, matching `entire-plugin.yml` and the command
+  `entire graph`. Do not tell users to run `entire plugin install entire-graph`;
+  a bare argument is a plugin-index name, not a repository or executable name.
+- Move repository-URL installs, source builds, updates, pinning, migration, and
+  platform-specific troubleshooting to operations documentation.
+
+### 3. Activate Entire Graph for the agent
+
+- State that activation is per repository. Before the command, disclose that it:
+  - writes `.entire/graph-agent.md`;
+  - creates or updates marker-delimited sections in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`;
+  - updates its managed blocks on later runs rather than appending duplicates.
+
+  Then show the exact command from the repository root:
+
+  ```sh
+  entire graph init-agents --repo .
+  ```
+
+- Tell the reader to review the three generated or updated files. Recommend
+  committing them as one setup change when the instructions should apply to the
+  team. Make the cache consequence explicit: while any of these indexable
+  Markdown files remains dirty or untracked, default working-tree queries bypass
+  cache reuse for the repository.
+- Link the guide emitted by `entire graph agent-guide`, but do not imply that every
+  client imports the referenced file the same way.
+- Require a fresh client task/session after activation. Use tested client-specific
+  language: for example, a new Codex task rooted at the repository rather than a
+  vague instruction to “restart.”
+- Name only clients whose instruction discovery has been tested. The detailed
+  client matrix must cover instruction precedence or shadowing, size limits,
+  whether the referenced guide is imported or read on demand, and how a user can
+  see that it loaded.
+- Test the Claude Code layout where `CLAUDE.md` already imports `AGENTS.md`.
+  `init-agents` writes the same pointer block to both files, so that layout can
+  import the guide twice; document the supported resolution rather than hiding it.
+- Document removal or reversal only if a supported procedure exists; do not invent one.
+
+### 4. First agent task and observable verification
+
+- Use a repository task in the user's own words, not an `entire graph` command,
+  as the first-use example. The reusable prompt shape is:
+
+  > Without changing repository source files, find where `<known feature>` is
+  > implemented, identify what calls it or what changing it would affect, and
+  > cite the relevant source.
+
+- Capture the concrete transcript in a clean consuming fixture with no pre-existing
+  Entire Graph instructions. Pin the fixture commit and commit the generated
+  activation files before recording so the example is reproducible and does not
+  confound instruction adoption with dirty-tree cache bypass.
+- Show only visible events: the prompt, instruction-file discovery, the graph
+  shell command and abbreviated result, the focused source read, any purposeful
+  relation or impact query, and the sourced answer. Do not expose or fabricate
+  hidden reasoning.
+- Require graph search before broad repository scanning, not before instruction
+  discovery or other client startup work.
+- Separate the verification layers:
+  - installation: `entire version` and `entire graph version` succeed;
+  - activation: the three expected files exist, the generated guide matches
+    `entire graph agent-guide`, their managed markers are intact, and the selected
+    client reports or demonstrates that the guide loaded;
+  - adoption: the fresh agent session visibly calls the graph before broad source
+    exploration;
+  - grounding: the answer is checked against focused source and, for a change,
+    the narrowest relevant test.
+- Do not hand-write plausible-looking output.
+
+### 5. Common agent tasks and cache behavior
+
+Use one small prompt-first table. Commands describe what the agent invokes; they
+are not the primary call to action.
+
+| Goal | Ask the agent | Graph operation |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Find code for a task | “Find where … is implemented.” | `search` |
+| Understand one definition | “Show and explain the definition of …” | `def` |
+| Inspect callers and relations | “What calls …?” | `neighbors` |
+| Estimate a symbol’s blast radius | “What would changing … affect?” | `impact` |
+| Review a commit or branch | “Summarize the semantic changes in …” | `commit` / `diff` |
+| Export the graph | “Export the graph for …” | `snapshot` |
+
+Follow the table with a short cache explanation:
+
+- The interactive query family (`search`, `def`, `explain`, `neighbors`, and
+  `impact`) reads the working tree by default, so current edits are visible.
+  Whole-graph streams and ref-based analysis have different defaults; link their
+  exact semantics instead of generalizing.
+- A graph-relevant clean working tree can reuse a tree- and option-keyed snapshot.
+  Any dirty graph-relevant path disables reuse for the whole working-tree query;
+  a changed committed tree produces a different entry.
+- Cache writes are derivative local state, so “repository-source-read-only” does
+  not mean “writes nothing.”
+- The installed guide's default `search` output is JSON and exposes
+  `index_cache_hit`. `--format agent` exposes a compact cache header. Do not claim
+  that `search --format text` reports cache state.
+- Link optional committed-tree prewarming, cache locations, overrides, and
+  cleanup limitations to operations. State there that `index` warms only the
+  committed-`HEAD` namespace, not the default working-tree namespace.
+- Reconcile the cache-directory fallback differences in `def` and `explain`
+  before making a universal cache-location claim.
+
+Do not copy flag catalogs or cache-internals prose into the root README.
+
+### 6. Agent flow, boundaries, and limits
+
+Use one compact flow that makes the agent—not the console—the recommended interface:
+
+```text
+user prompt → coding agent → repository instructions → entire graph CLI
+            → ranked graph evidence → focused source/test check → sourced answer
+```
+
+Add a concise boundary summary:
+
+- Built-in analysis is local and no-egress; installation obtains software.
+- Queries may write derivative caches, and `init-agents` writes the three disclosed
+  repository instruction files.
+- Static relations and dependent counts are not compiler-accurate. Calls, routes,
+  tools, renames, dynamic dispatch, reflection, generated code, and runtime wiring
+  can be heuristic or incomplete.
+- Unsupported languages are inventory-only or produce explicit partial failures.
+- Working-tree and committed-tree defaults differ by command family.
+- Entire Graph is a one-shot CLI and semantic provider. Entire Brain is the
+  separate durable consumer and MCP surface; Entire Graph is not a daemon,
+  watcher, hosted memory system, or MCP server.
+
+Link the full language, trust, command, and Brain/Graph boundary documents rather
+than embedding a complete trust matrix in the landing page.
+
+### 7. Documentation and manual use
+
+- End with a short documentation map organized by user intent.
+- Put direct CLI examples and automation in the command and operations references,
+  labeled as manual or programmatic alternatives to the agent flow.
+- Keep quantitative methodology, environments, corrections, and reproduction in
+  `docs/benchmarks.md`. Include no root benchmark number unless it survives the
+  claim audit and materially helps a new reader decide whether to continue.
+- Include development, issue/support, and license links. Add a security link only
+  if a real reporting policy exists.
+
+## Document migration
+
+Use this table as the canonical destination map; do not create two authorities
+for the same subject.
+
+| File | Action | Canonical role |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `README.md` | Rewrite in place; never rename | Agent-first landing page described above |
+| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.entire/graph-agent.md` | Regenerate or reconcile, then validate together | Current repository-agent instructions with no dangling or duplicate imports, stale limits, or universal safety claims |
+| `entire-plugin.yml` | Track as a separate release prerequisite | Product description consistent with agent-first repository intelligence rather than checkpoint-only positioning |
+| `docs/README.md` | Retain and update | User-intent index and explicit archive boundary |

+# Entire Graph README A+ Plan
+
+Status: Draft for editing
+
+## Objective
+
+Turn the root README into a concise, credible landing page that lets a reader:
+
+1. Understand what Entire Graph is and is not.
+2. Install the prerequisite Entire CLI and the Entire Graph plugin.
+3. Activate Entire Graph for a coding agent with explicit repository side effects.
+4. Ask the agent a repository-source-read-only code question and verify that it
+   used graph evidence before inspecting focused source.
+5. Understand cache reuse and freshness, limits, data flow, and side effects.
+6. Reach detailed documentation without searching through the repository.
+
+This is a documentation-only project. It does not change CLI behavior, graph
+semantics, benchmarks, releases, the plugin catalog, or integrations.
+
+## Fixed assumptions
+
+- Keep the root filename exactly `README.md`.
+- At publication time, the official plugin index contains `graph` and a clean
+  `entire plugin install graph` succeeds on every platform the README claims.
+- Entire CLI 0.10.0 or later is already available through its documented
+  installation channels.
+- Setup uses the console, but day-to-day code discovery and analysis happen
+  through the coding agent in response to repository tasks.
+- Direct CLI use remains available for debugging, automation, and downstream tools;
+  it is not the primary user journey.
+
+## Open decisions
+
+- Which coding-agent clients have a tested instruction-loading and verification
+  path that the root README may name?
+- Which clean consuming fixture and pinned commit will produce the checked agent
+  transcript?
+- Which platforms will the installation example explicitly claim to support?
+- Is any quantitative result relevant enough for the root README? Default to none
+  unless one survives the claim audit.
+
+## Guiding principles
+
+- Make the recommended usage journey agent-first: setup installs and activates
+  Entire Graph, then the coding agent performs graph queries during repository work.
+- Disclose repository writes before asking the user to run `init-agents`, then
+  demonstrate the workflow with a repository-source-read-only task.
+- Prefer real commands, output, limits, and failure modes over adjectives.
+- Keep one canonical home for each substantial topic.
+- Scope every claim precisely; avoid absolutes such as “every,” “always,” and “zero” unless the contract proves them.
+- Keep benchmark evidence visible but move methodology and historical corrections out of the landing page.
+- Judge README length by usefulness, not an arbitrary line count.
+- Preserve existing URLs where practical; use compatibility pointers when documents move.
+
+## Competitor-informed requirements
+
+The comparison with [Graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/7fe58b0b0f3873be9a21c30106b8b8527c353aa6/README.md),
+[codebase-memory-mcp](https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/blob/d150ebe4fc78a9a3f85013d2087a849e5d59eb0f/README.md),
+[Mem0](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/96d45b78c702b742fc91a2ce9eae91805be9144b/README.md),
+[Graphiti](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/b2ff2eadd9a6b75a261a5cf0b19557883a13f752/README.md), and
+[Supermemory](https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/blob/82dae50ef458139823b3bfd3ebaaaac90ffd8a7c/README.md)
+produces four requirements:
+
+- Make a natural-language task—not a graph command—the first useful action.
+- Show observable agent events, focused source evidence, and the resulting answer;
+  never end the quickstart at “installed” or “done.”
+- Separate installation, instruction loading, graph adoption, and answer grounding
+  so users can verify each layer independently.
+- Keep reference material out of the landing page and label direct console use as
+  manual, diagnostic, or automation-oriented.
+
+## Target root README structure
+
+### 1. Hero and primary action
+
+- One short category sentence, for example: "Entire Graph is a local
+  static-analysis plugin that helps coding agents find definitions,
+  relationships, and change impact in Git repositories."
+- One supporting line can name tree-sitter and the main evidence types without
+  forcing every capability and audience into the opening sentence.
+- State the built-in analyzer’s no-egress boundary without implying that
+  installation itself is offline.
+- Make the primary journey explicit: install → activate for an agent → ask a
+  code question → inspect the evidence.
+- Link directly to installation, the first agent task, manual CLI use,
+  documentation, and limitations.
+- Avoid badge walls, slogans, release announcements, and unsupported superlatives.
+
+### 2. Prerequisites and installation
+

+  `entire` 0.10.0 or later must already be installed and on `PATH`. Version
+  0.10.0 is the first stable Entire CLI release with remote name/URL plugin
+  installation.
+- Show the common macOS/Linux Entire CLI installation before the Entire Graph
+  installation:
+
+  ```sh
+  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
+  entire version
+  ```
+
+- Link other platforms and installation methods to the current
+  [Entire CLI installation documentation](https://docs.entire.io/installation)
+  instead of copying every platform command into this README.

+- Document removal or reversal only if a supported procedure exists; do not invent one.
+
+### 4. First agent task and observable verification
+
+- Use a repository task in the user's own words, not an `entire graph` command,
+  as the first-use example. The reusable prompt shape is:
+
+  > Without changing repository source files, find where `<known feature>` is
+  > implemented, identify what calls it or what changing it would affect, and
+  > cite the relevant source.
+

+  Entire Graph instructions. Pin the fixture commit and commit the generated
+  activation files before recording so the example is reproducible and does not
+  confound instruction adoption with dirty-tree cache bypass.

+  shell command and abbreviated result, the focused source read, any purposeful
+  relation or impact query, and the sourced answer. Do not expose or fabricate

+  discovery or other client startup work.
+- Separate the verification layers:
+  - installation: `entire version` and `entire graph version` succeed;
+  - activation: the three expected files exist, the generated guide matches
+    `entire graph agent-guide`, their managed markers are intact, and the selected
+    client reports or demonstrates that the guide loaded;
+  - adoption: the fresh agent session visibly calls the graph before broad source
+    exploration;
+  - grounding: the answer is checked against focused source and, for a change,
+    the narrowest relevant test.
+- Do not hand-write plausible-looking output.
+
+### 5. Common agent tasks and cache behavior
+
+Use one small prompt-first table. Commands describe what the agent invokes; they
+are not the primary call to action.
+
+| Goal | Ask the agent | Graph operation |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Find code for a task | “Find where … is implemented.” | `search` |
+| Understand one definition | “Show and explain the definition of …” | `def` |
+| Inspect callers and relations | “What calls …?” | `neighbors` |
+| Estimate a symbol’s blast radius | “What would changing … affect?” | `impact` |
+| Review a commit or branch | “Summarize the semantic changes in …” | `commit` / `diff` |
+| Export the graph | “Export the graph for …” | `snapshot` |
+
+Follow the table with a short cache explanation:
+
+- The interactive query family (`search`, `def`, `explain`, `neighbors`, and
+  `impact`) reads the working tree by default, so current edits are visible.
+  Whole-graph streams and ref-based analysis have different defaults; link their
+  exact semantics instead of generalizing.
+- A graph-relevant clean working tree can reuse a tree- and option-keyed snapshot.
+  Any dirty graph-relevant path disables reuse for the whole working-tree query;
+  a changed committed tree produces a different entry.
+- Cache writes are derivative local state, so “repository-source-read-only” does
+  not mean “writes nothing.”
+- The installed guide's default `search` output is JSON and exposes
+  `index_cache_hit`. `--format agent` exposes a compact cache header. Do not claim
+  that `search --format text` reports cache state.
+- Link optional committed-tree prewarming, cache locations, overrides, and
+  cleanup limitations to operations. State there that `index` warms only the
+  committed-`HEAD` namespace, not the default working-tree namespace.
+- Reconcile the cache-directory fallback differences in `def` and `explain`
+  before making a universal cache-location claim.
+
+Do not copy flag catalogs or cache-internals prose into the root README.
+
+### 6. Agent flow, boundaries, and limits
+
+Use one compact flow that makes the agent—not the console—the recommended interface:
+
+```text
+user prompt → coding agent → repository instructions → entire graph CLI
+            → ranked graph evidence → focused source/test check → sourced answer
+```
+
+Add a concise boundary summary:
+
+- Built-in analysis is local and no-egress; installation obtains software.
+- Queries may write derivative caches, and `init-agents` writes the three disclosed
+  repository instruction files.
+- Static relations and dependent counts are not compiler-accurate. Calls, routes,
+  tools, renames, dynamic dispatch, reflection, generated code, and runtime wiring
+  can be heuristic or incomplete.
+- Unsupported languages are inventory-only or produce explicit partial failures.
+- Working-tree and committed-tree defaults differ by command family.
+- Entire Graph is a one-shot CLI and semantic provider. Entire Brain is the
+  separate durable consumer and MCP surface; Entire Graph is not a daemon,
+  watcher, hosted memory system, or MCP server.
+
+Link the full language, trust, command, and Brain/Graph boundary documents rather
+than embedding a complete trust matrix in the landing page.
+
+### 7. Documentation and manual use
+
+- End with a short documentation map organized by user intent.
+- Put direct CLI examples and automation in the command and operations references,
+  labeled as manual or programmatic alternatives to the agent flow.
+- Keep quantitative methodology, environments, corrections, and reproduction in
+  `docs/benchmarks.md`. Include no root benchmark number unless it survives the
+  claim audit and materially helps a new reader decide whether to continue.

 func TestImportCapabilityMatchesScannerRegistry(t *testing.T) {
 	for extension := range importScanners {
 		if !importCapableExtension(extension) {
 			t.Errorf("%s has an import scanner but is not reported import-capable", extension)
 		}
 		// Empty content must yield no imports rather than panicking: the scanners
 		// run over whatever the reader returns, including a file it could not read.

 	// Extensions that parse but carry no imports must stay non-capable; a
 	// nil-returning scanner entry would silently make them capable.
 	for _, extension := range []string{".hcl", ".tf", ".tfvars", ".sql", ".yaml", ".md", ".json"} {
 		if importCapableExtension(extension) {
 			t.Errorf("%s has no import scanner but is reported import-capable", extension)

 			t.Errorf("%s returned imports %v despite having no scanner", extension, got)
 		}
 	}
 }

 # Entire Graph
 
 **This release is for your agents.**
 
 Entire Graph gives coding agents a precomputed, deterministic map of your codebase — every
 function, type, route, and call relationship — so they can start from ranked


 QA accuracy means the share of questions answered correctly. Recall@10 means
 the share for which the evidence-bearing conversation appears among the first
 ten retrieved results. A score such as 0.914 is 91.4%.
 
 ## Evidence status
 
 The former 54.9% Haiku, 57.7% Sonnet, and 31–73% open-model token-savings
 figures are withdrawn. They were token-first measurements under a prompt policy
 that encouraged the graph arms to stop early and did not require equivalent
 resolution evidence from every arm. “Patch produced” was also reported as task

 A replacement claim requires:

 - each tool's normal interface;
 - official task resolution as the primary outcome;
 - token and turn comparisons over commonly resolved tasks;

 ### Compact snapshot artifact
 
 `entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson` remains the interoperable default: it is the existing object-per-line stream. For a complete, local compact artifact, use:
 
 ```sh
 entire graph snapshot --repo . --format compact-ndjson > graph.compact.ndjson
 entire graph snapshot-query --input graph.compact.ndjson --symbol Cache.Refresh --format ndjson
 entire graph snapshot-query --input graph.compact.ndjson --from '<stable-id>' --relation CALLS --format ndjson
 ```
 
 Compact NDJSON v1 is full-snapshot-only; targeted `--to`, `--from`, and `--relation` output stays native NDJSON. Its first `h` line is the only version marker, dictionary `d` lines are part of the artifact and its raw byte count, and unknown versions are rejected. The compact and native streams must have the same decoded public projection and canonical semantic SHA-256; hash equality alone is not a losslessness proof. +# Entire Graph README A+ Plan
+
+Status: Draft for editing
+
+## Objective
+
+Turn the root README into a concise, credible landing page that lets a reader:
+
+1. Understand what Entire Graph is and is not.
+2. Install the prerequisite Entire CLI and the Entire Graph plugin.
+3. Activate Entire Graph for a coding agent with explicit repository side effects.
+4. Ask the agent a repository-source-read-only code question and verify that it
+   used graph evidence before inspecting focused source.
+5. Understand cache reuse and freshness, limits, data flow, and side effects.
+6. Reach detailed documentation without searching through the repository.
+
+This is a documentation-only project. It does not change CLI behavior, graph
+semantics, benchmarks, releases, the plugin catalog, or integrations.
+
+## Fixed assumptions
+
+- Keep the root filename exactly `README.md`.
+- At publication time, the official plugin index contains `graph` and a clean
+  `entire plugin install graph` succeeds on every platform the README claims.
+- Entire CLI 0.10.0 or later is already available through its documented
+  installation channels.
+- Setup uses the console, but day-to-day code discovery and analysis happen
+  through the coding agent in response to repository tasks.
+- Direct CLI use remains available for debugging, automation, and downstream tools;
+  it is not the primary user journey.
+
+## Open decisions
+
+- Which coding-agent clients have a tested instruction-loading and verification
+  path that the root README may name?
+- Which clean consuming fixture and pinned commit will produce the checked agent
+  transcript?
+- Which platforms will the installation example explicitly claim to support?
+- Is any quantitative result relevant enough for the root README? Default to none
+  unless one survives the claim audit.
+
+## Guiding principles
+
+- Make the recommended usage journey agent-first: setup installs and activates
+  Entire Graph, then the coding agent performs graph queries during repository work.
+- Disclose repository writes before asking the user to run `init-agents`, then
+  demonstrate the workflow with a repository-source-read-only task.
+- Prefer real commands, output, limits, and failure modes over adjectives.
+- Keep one canonical home for each substantial topic.
+- Scope every claim precisely; avoid absolutes such as “every,” “always,” and “zero” unless the contract proves them.
+- Keep benchmark evidence visible but move methodology and historical corrections out of the landing page.
+- Judge README length by usefulness, not an arbitrary line count.
+- Preserve existing URLs where practical; use compatibility pointers when documents move.
+
+## Competitor-informed requirements
+
+The comparison with [Graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/7fe58b0b0f3873be9a21c30106b8b8527c353aa6/README.md),
+[codebase-memory-mcp](https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/blob/d150ebe4fc78a9a3f85013d2087a849e5d59eb0f/README.md),
+[Mem0](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/96d45b78c702b742fc91a2ce9eae91805be9144b/README.md),
+[Graphiti](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/b2ff2eadd9a6b75a261a5cf0b19557883a13f752/README.md), and
+[Supermemory](https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/blob/82dae50ef458139823b3bfd3ebaaaac90ffd8a7c/README.md)
+produces four requirements:
+
+- Make a natural-language task—not a graph command—the first useful action.
+- Show observable agent events, focused source evidence, and the resulting answer;
+  never end the quickstart at “installed” or “done.”
+- Separate installation, instruction loading, graph adoption, and answer grounding
+  so users can verify each layer independently.
+- Keep reference material out of the landing page and label direct console use as
+  manual, diagnostic, or automation-oriented.
+

 # Entire Graph
 
 **This release is for your agents.**
 
 Entire Graph gives coding agents a precomputed, deterministic map of your codebase — every
 function, type, route, and call relationship — so they can start from ranked
 structural evidence instead of broad grep-and-read exploration. It is 100% local:
 no network, no model calls, no keys.
 
 ## Install (one minute)
 
-Go 1.24+ and a C compiler required first
+Go 1.26 and a C compiler required first
 
 ```sh
 go install github.com/entireio/entire-graph/cmd/entire-graph@main
 entire plugin install "$(go env GOBIN | grep . || echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin")/entire-graph" --force
 ```
 
 Then, in any repo your agents work in:
 
 ```sh
 entire graph init-agents
 ```
 
 That's it. `init-agents` drops the operating guide into your project's `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`,
 so Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Pi — any agent that reads those files — picks up the
 search-first workflow automatically. No config, no MCP server, no daemon.

 ## Evidence status
 
 The former 54.9% Haiku, 57.7% Sonnet, and 31–73% open-model token-savings
 figures are withdrawn. They were token-first measurements under a prompt policy
 that encouraged the graph arms to stop early and did not require equivalent
 resolution evidence from every arm. “Patch produced” was also reported as task
 completion, which is not the same as passing the task's tests.
 
 A replacement claim requires:
 
 - identical tool-agnostic working instructions across arms;
 - each tool's normal interface;
 - official task resolution as the primary outcome;
 - token and turn comparisons over commonly resolved tasks;
 - repeated runs with uncertainty; and
 - pinned binaries, prompts, datasets, and retained raw artifacts.
 
 Until that evidence is frozen, `entire graph stats` and the status line are
 local heuristic reports only, not benchmark results.
 
 ## More
 
 ### Compact snapshot artifact
 
 `entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson` remains the interoperable default: it is the existing object-per-line stream. For a complete, local compact artifact, use:
 
 ```sh
 entire graph snapshot --repo . --format compact-ndjson > graph.compact.ndjson
 entire graph snapshot-query --input graph.compact.ndjson --symbol Cache.Refresh --format ndjson
 entire graph snapshot-query --input graph.compact.ndjson --from '<stable-id>' --relation CALLS --format ndjson
 ```
 
 Compact NDJSON v1 is full-snapshot-only; targeted `--to`, `--from`, and `--relation` output stays native NDJSON. Its first `h` line is the only version marker, dictionary `d` lines are part of the artifact and its raw byte count, and unknown versions are rejected. The compact and native streams must have the same decoded public projection and canonical semantic SHA-256; hash equality alone is not a losslessness proof. Compact cache entries use a separate namespace from native snapshot entries.

+# Entire Graph README A+ Plan
+
+Status: Draft for editing
+
+## Objective
+
+Turn the root README into a concise, credible landing page that lets a reader:
+
+1. Understand what Entire Graph is and is not.
+2. Install the prerequisite Entire CLI and the Entire Graph plugin.
+3. Activate Entire Graph for a coding agent with explicit repository side effects.
+4. Ask the agent a repository-source-read-only code question and verify that it
+   used graph evidence before inspecting focused source.
+5. Understand cache reuse and freshness, limits, data flow, and side effects.
+6. Reach detailed documentation without searching through the repository.
+
+This is a documentation-only project. It does not change CLI behavior, graph
+semantics, benchmarks, releases, the plugin catalog, or integrations.
+
+## Fixed assumptions
+
+- Keep the root filename exactly `README.md`.
+- At publication time, the official plugin index contains `graph` and a clean
+  `entire plugin install graph` succeeds on every platform the README claims.
+- Entire CLI 0.10.0 or later is already available through its documented
+  installation channels.
+- Setup uses the console, but day-to-day code discovery and analysis happen
+  through the coding agent in response to repository tasks.
+- Direct CLI use remains available for debugging, automation, and downstream tools;
+  it is not the primary user journey.
+
+## Open decisions
+
+- Which coding-agent clients have a tested instruction-loading and verification
+  path that the root README may name?
+- Which clean consuming fixture and pinned commit will produce the checked agent
+  transcript?
+- Which platforms will the installation example explicitly claim to support?
+- Is any quantitative result relevant enough for the root README? Default to none
+  unless one survives the claim audit.
+
+## Guiding principles
+
+- Make the recommended usage journey agent-first: setup installs and activates
+  Entire Graph, then the coding agent performs graph queries during repository work.
+- Disclose repository writes before asking the user to run `init-agents`, then
+  demonstrate the workflow with a repository-source-read-only task.
+- Prefer real commands, output, limits, and failure modes over adjectives.
+- Keep one canonical home for each substantial topic.
+- Scope every claim precisely; avoid absolutes such as “every,” “always,” and “zero” unless the contract proves them.
+- Keep benchmark evidence visible but move methodology and historical corrections out of the landing page.
+- Judge README length by usefulness, not an arbitrary line count.
+- Preserve existing URLs where practical; use compatibility pointers when documents move.
+
+## Competitor-informed requirements
+
+The comparison with [Graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/7fe58b0b0f3873be9a21c30106b8b8527c353aa6/README.md),
+[codebase-memory-mcp](https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/blob/d150ebe4fc78a9a3f85013d2087a849e5d59eb0f/README.md),
+[Mem0](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/96d45b78c702b742fc91a2ce9eae91805be9144b/README.md),
+[Graphiti](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/b2ff2eadd9a6b75a261a5cf0b19557883a13f752/README.md), and
+[Supermemory](https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/blob/82dae50ef458139823b3bfd3ebaaaac90ffd8a7c/README.md)
+produces four requirements:
+
+- Make a natural-language task—not a graph command—the first useful action.
+- Show observable agent events, focused source evidence, and the resulting answer;
+  never end the quickstart at “installed” or “done.”
+- Separate installation, instruction loading, graph adoption, and answer grounding
+  so users can verify each layer independently.
+- Keep reference material out of the landing page and label direct console use as
+  manual, diagnostic, or automation-oriented.
+
+## Target root README structure
+
+### 1. Hero and primary action
+
+- One short category sentence, for example: "Entire Graph is a local
+  static-analysis plugin that helps coding agents find definitions,
+  relationships, and change impact in Git repositories."
+- One supporting line can name tree-sitter and the main evidence types without
+  forcing every capability and audience into the opening sentence.
+- State the built-in analyzer’s no-egress boundary without implying that
+  installation itself is offline.
+- Make the primary journey explicit: install → activate for an agent → ask a
+  code question → inspect the evidence.
+- Link directly to installation, the first agent task, manual CLI use,
+  documentation, and limitations.
+- Avoid badge walls, slogans, release announcements, and unsupported superlatives.

+  import the guide twice; document the supported resolution rather than hiding it.
+- Document removal or reversal only if a supported procedure exists; do not invent one.
+
+### 4. First agent task and observable verification
+
+- Use a repository task in the user's own words, not an `entire graph` command,
+  as the first-use example. The reusable prompt shape is:
+
+  > Without changing repository source files, find where `<known feature>` is
+  > implemented, identify what calls it or what changing it would affect, and
+  > cite the relevant source.
+
+- Capture the concrete transcript in a clean consuming fixture with no pre-existing
+  Entire Graph instructions. Pin the fixture commit and commit the generated
+  activation files before recording so the example is reproducible and does not
+  confound instruction adoption with dirty-tree cache bypass.
+- Show only visible events: the prompt, instruction-file discovery, the graph
+  shell command and abbreviated result, the focused source read, any purposeful
+  relation or impact query, and the sourced answer. Do not expose or fabricate
+  hidden reasoning.
+- Require graph search before broad repository scanning, not before instruction
+  discovery or other client startup work.
+- Separate the verification layers:
+  - installation: `entire version` and `entire graph version` succeed;
+  - activation: the three expected files exist, the generated guide matches
+    `entire graph agent-guide`, their managed markers are intact, and the selected
+    client reports or demonstrates that the guide loaded;
+  - adoption: the fresh agent session visibly calls the graph before broad source
+    exploration;
+  - grounding: the answer is checked against focused source and, for a change,
+    the narrowest relevant test.
+- Do not hand-write plausible-looking output.
+
+### 5. Common agent tasks and cache behavior
+
+Use one small prompt-first table. Commands describe what the agent invokes; they
+are not the primary call to action.
+
+| Goal | Ask the agent | Graph operation |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Find code for a task | “Find where … is implemented.” | `search` |
+| Understand one definition | “Show and explain the definition of …” | `def` |
+| Inspect callers and relations | “What calls …?” | `neighbors` |
+| Estimate a symbol’s blast radius | “What would changing … affect?” | `impact` |
+| Review a commit or branch | “Summarize the semantic changes in …” | `commit` / `diff` |
+| Export the graph | “Export the graph for …” | `snapshot` |
+
+Follow the table with a short cache explanation:
+
+- The interactive query family (`search`, `def`, `explain`, `neighbors`, and
+  `impact`) reads the working tree by default, so current edits are visible.
+  Whole-graph streams and ref-based analysis have different defaults; link their
+  exact semantics instead of generalizing.
+- A graph-relevant clean working tree can reuse a tree- and option-keyed snapshot.
+  Any dirty graph-relevant path disables reuse for the whole working-tree query;
+  a changed committed tree produces a different entry.
+- Cache writes are derivative local state, so “repository-source-read-only” does
+  not mean “writes nothing.”
+- The installed guide's default `search` output is JSON and exposes
+  `index_cache_hit`. `--format agent` exposes a compact cache header. Do not claim
+  that `search --format text` reports cache state.
+- Link optional committed-tree prewarming, cache locations, overrides, and
+  cleanup limitations to operations. State there that `index` warms only the
+  committed-`HEAD` namespace, not the default working-tree namespace.
+- Reconcile the cache-directory fallback differences in `def` and `explain`
+  before making a universal cache-location claim.
+
+Do not copy flag catalogs or cache-internals prose into the root README.
+
+### 6. Agent flow, boundaries, and limits
+
+Use one compact flow that makes the agent—not the console—the recommended interface:
+
+```text
+user prompt → coding agent → repository instructions → entire graph CLI
+            → ranked graph evidence → focused source/test check → sourced answer
+```
+
+Add a concise boundary summary:
+
+- Built-in analysis is local and no-egress; installation obtains software.
+- Queries may write derivative caches, and `init-agents` writes the three disclosed
+  repository instruction files.
+- Static relations and dependent counts are not compiler-accurate. Calls, routes,
+  tools, renames, dynamic dispatch, reflection, generated code, and runtime wiring
+  can be heuristic or incomplete.
+- Unsupported languages are inventory-only or produce explicit partial failures.
+- Working-tree and committed-tree defaults differ by command family.
+- Entire Graph is a one-shot CLI and semantic provider. Entire Brain is the
+  separate durable consumer and MCP surface; Entire Graph is not a daemon,
+  watcher, hosted memory system, or MCP server.
+
+Link the full language, trust, command, and Brain/Graph boundary documents rather
+than embedding a complete trust matrix in the landing page.
+
+### 7. Documentation and manual use

+- End with a short documentation map organized by user intent.
+- Put direct CLI examples and automation in the command and operations references,
+  labeled as manual or programmatic alternatives to the agent flow.
+- Keep quantitative methodology, environments, corrections, and reproduction in

+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- [ ] A new reader can identify the product category, input, output, audience, and principal boundary from the first screen.
+- [ ] The first-run sequence installs and verifies the Entire CLI, installs and
+  verifies Entire Graph, discloses and performs agent activation, then
+  demonstrates useful output through a repository-source-read-only agent task.
+- [ ] In a clean environment, `entire plugin install graph` resolves through the
+  default index and makes `entire graph version` succeed.
+- [ ] The root README never uses `entire-graph` as a bare plugin-index name and
+  never presents `--yes`, `--force`, `@main`, or a local build as the recommended
+  first install.
+- [ ] Activation is explicitly per repository, shows the exact command and three
+  file effects before execution, and tells the user how to review and optionally

+- [ ] Limitations cover heuristic analysis, inventory-only languages, partial

 	}

 // TestImportCapabilityMatchesScannerRegistry pins the property that replaced a
 // hand-maintained mirror: every extension with an import scanner is reported as
 // import-capable, and every extension without one is not. The two used to be
 // separate switch statements kept in sync by a comment.
 func TestImportCapabilityMatchesScannerRegistry(t *testing.T) {
 	for extension := range importScanners {
 		if !importCapableExtension(extension) {
 			t.Errorf("%s has an import scanner but is not reported import-capable", extension)
 		}
 		// Empty content must yield no imports rather than panicking: the scanners
 		// run over whatever the reader returns, including a file it could not read.
 		if got := importsFor("file"+extension, ""); len(got) != 0 {
 			t.Errorf("%s scanner returned %v for empty content", extension, got)
 		}
 	}
 	// Extensions that parse but carry no imports must stay non-capable; a
 	// nil-returning scanner entry would silently make them capable.
 	for _, extension := range []string{".hcl", ".tf", ".tfvars", ".sql", ".yaml", ".md", ".json"} {
 		if importCapableExtension(extension) {
 			t.Errorf("%s has no import scanner but is reported import-capable", extension)
 		}
 		if got := importsFor("file"+extension, "import x\nuse y;\n#include <z>\n"); len(got) != 0 {
 			t.Errorf("%s returned imports %v despite having no scanner", extension, got)
 		}
 	}
 }

+		t.Fatalf("semantic provider requirements no longer document heuristic_relation_types")

 		t.Fatalf("heuristic_relation_types list is unterminated")

 	documented := map[string]bool{}

 			documented[name] = true
 		}
 	}

    77	// One command issues several snapshot lookups (graph scope, complete preindex,
    78	// selective build) and must not pay for a `git status` each time; a window this
    79	// short cannot span an edit that happens between two of them, while a
    80	// long-lived library consumer still re-checks on every new command.
    81	const worktreeCleanTTL = 2 * time.Second
    82

    84		clean     bool
    85		checkedAt time.Time
    86	}

    89	
    90	// absOrRepo resolves repo to an absolute path, falling back to the input when
    91	// that is impossible. It exists so a cleanliness verdict is memoized under the
    92	// same key the cache lookups use.
    93	func absOrRepo(repo string) string {
    94		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(repo); err == nil {

    98	}

   108	// scratch — and it never hides a dirty edit, because a dirty indexable file
   109	// fails the check and bypasses the cache exactly as before.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/audit_plan_consistency
Payload:
- **Blocker — The documented install path depends on release work explicitly excluded from scope.** Plan lines 17–18, 23–24, 340–341, 403–404, and 443–444 require `entire plugin install graph` to install the demonstrated functionality while excluding index and release publication. Currently, `entire plugin search graph` returns no match, the latest tag is `v0.2.0`, and the [v0.2.0 release](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/releases/tag/v0.2.0) has no assets. Moreover, `git show v0.2.0:internal/cli/root.go` lines 49–83 lacks `init-agents`, while current [root.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/root.go:92) adds the required command family. The repository’s release process only creates local archives ([release.sh](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/scripts/release.sh:27), [operations.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/operations.md:31)) and explicitly does not publish them ([operations.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/operations.md:53)). Add a named, owned prerequisite for a new compatible release, checksum-backed assets, and the index entry; gate README publication on it rather than treating it as an assumption.

- **High — The Claude duplicate-import requirement contradicts current `init-agents` behavior and the documentation-only non-goal.** Plan lines 148–150 acknowledge that `CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md` can import the guide twice, but lines 344–346, 372–373, and 411–413 require zero duplicate imports, while lines 448–450 exclude changing `init-agents`. The repository already demonstrates the conflict: [CLAUDE.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/CLAUDE.md:1) imports `AGENTS.md` and also directly imports the guide at [line 3](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/CLAUDE.md:3); [AGENTS.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/AGENTS.md:201) imports the same guide. The implementation unconditionally writes the pointer block to both files ([agents.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/agents.go:107)). Either accept and document duplicate loading, define a durable supported manual layout, or make import-aware `init-agents` behavior an explicit product prerequisite.

- **Medium — Activation side effects and idempotence are overstated.** Plan lines 123–138 and 408–410 promise explicit effects and later updates without duplicate blocks. In reality, `.entire/graph-agent.md` is overwritten wholesale on every run ([agents.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/agents.go:98)), and block replacement handles only the first well-formed begin/end pair ([agents.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/agents.go:124)); malformed markers or pre-existing duplicate blocks fall through or leave duplicates ([agents.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/agents.go:132)). Disclose the overwrite, scope idempotence to one intact managed block, and document malformed/duplicate recovery—or track stronger behavior as a product prerequisite.

- **Medium — The superseding cache ADR destination is incomplete, leaving a stale document labeled authoritative.** Plan lines 278, 369, and 451–452 say to add an unnamed superseding ADR while preserving ADR 0002, but do not require updating ADR 0002’s status/backlink. The current docs index still names ADR 0002 as the cache source of truth ([docs/README.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/README.md:33)); ADR 0002 remains “Accepted” ([0002-committed-tree-cache-key.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/adr/0002-committed-tree-cache-key.md:3)) and says working-tree mode is uncached ([line 134](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/adr/0002-committed-tree-cache-key.md:134)), while current code caches eligible clean worktrees ([search_cache.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/search_cache.go:135)). Name the new ADR path, mark ADR 0002 superseded with a forward link, and update the docs index/source-of-truth row explicitly.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/audit_cache_claims
Payload:
- High — `--head` is not end-to-end committed-tree output for three interactive commands, and `explain` mislabels it. This blocks the “exact semantics” work in plan lines 199–202, 349–351, and 425–426 unless tracked as the product prerequisite contemplated at 448–450.
  - `neighbors` loads the selected snapshot, then annotates it from the live filesystem: `internal/cli/neighbors.go:153-168`; `newRepoLineReader` reads disk via `os.OpenRoot`: `internal/cli/callsite.go:83-124`.
  - `impact` does the same: `internal/cli/impact.go:140-153`.
  - `def --head` resolves declarations from the snapshot but its default text/agent output calls `writeDefBodies`: `internal/cli/def.go:166-172,192-210`; those bodies use the live line reader: `internal/cli/def.go:223-239`, `internal/cli/symbolref.go:625-665`.
  - `explain --head` sets `Worktree=false` at `internal/cli/explain.go:358-361`, but all text/agent output uses the fixed header claiming “from the working tree”: `internal/cli/explain.go:280-290,330-336`.
  - Existing tests do not catch dirty-worktree/HEAD divergence: the HEAD neighbors test only checks cache telemetry (`internal/cli/neighbors_efficiency_test.go:13-61`), while the explain renderer test merely asserts the fixed header (`internal/cli/explain_test.go:77-90`).

- Medium — “any dirty graph-relevant path disables reuse” is too absolute in plan lines 203–205, 349–351, and 418–420. The bypass predicate only rejects dirty paths recognized as indexable or named resolver manifests: `internal/sem/search_cache.go:145-155`. Graph-shaping ignore inputs instead participate in the cache key: explicit ignore/include file contents at `internal/sem/search_cache.go:809-829`, and live `.graphignore` at `internal/sem/search_cache.go:831-845`. `TestSearchSnapshotKeyIncludesGraphIgnore` proves edits select a new key (`internal/sem/search_cache_test.go:1349-1381`), while `TestWorktreeSnapshotStillCachesWithUnindexableUntrackedFiles` proves some dirty paths retain reuse (`internal/sem/search_cache_worktree_test.go:181-215`). Documentation should distinguish whole-query bypass for dirty indexable/manifest paths from cache-key changes for graph-control files.

- Medium — prewarming is narrower than “the committed-HEAD namespace” suggests at plan lines 211–213, 349–351, and 421. `index` defaults to `full` (`internal/cli/index.go:181-183`), while bare `search --head` defaults to `fast` (`internal/cli/search.go:1718-1724`). Profile is part of the key (`internal/sem/search_cache.go:784-790`), as are the worktree marker and other options (`internal/sem/search_cache.go:797-845`). Thus default `index` does not warm bare `search --head`; it warms only matching HEAD/profile/options queries. It also cannot warm default worktree queries: `index` rejects `--worktree` (`internal/cli/index.go:230-233`), and the separate-view invariant is tested at `internal/sem/search_cache_worktree_test.go:112-139`.

- Medium — the cache telemetry wording at plan lines 208–210, 349–351, and 420 needs more precision.
  - The installed guide omits `--format`, so JSON is indeed selected (`internal/cli/agents.go:25-28`, `internal/cli/search.go:1718-1724`), but the exact JSON path is `stats.index_cache_hit`, not a top-level field: `internal/sem/search.go:389-392,446-449`.
  - Agent output does not have one fixed “compact header.” It prefers `Index: cache-{hit|miss} (...)` (`internal/cli/search.go:1072-1083`) and falls through several `I:{hit|miss}/...` forms as the byte budget tightens (`internal/cli/search.go:1130-1150,1205-1210`); the tight-budget test pins the compact prefix at `internal/cli/search_tight_budget_test.go:43-48`.
  - `false` is rendered as “miss” without distinguishing cold build, dirty-path bypass, `--no-cache`, or unavailable cache directory (`internal/cli/search.go:1072-1078`). The observable field/header cannot by itself prove why reuse did not occur.
  - The plan is correct that text output has no cache telemetry; `writeTextSearch` begins directly with diagnostics/results and never reads `IndexCacheHit`: `internal/cli/search.go:431-510`.

- Medium — plan lines 214–215 identify a real unresolved exception. `resolveCacheDir` provides flag → plugin-data-dir → platform-cache fallback (`internal/cli/env.go:40-66`), and search/neighbors/impact use it. `def` and `explain` instead stop after explicit flag or `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`: `internal/cli/def.go:161-172`, `internal/cli/explain.go:172-184`. In a direct invocation with neither set, they do not use the platform cache. Observability also differs: `def --format json` has top-level `index_cache_hit` (`internal/cli/def.go:125-145`), its default text output omits it (`internal/cli/def.go:192-210`), and `explain` discards the returned hit boolean while `ExplainResponse` has no cache fields (`internal/cli/explain.go:101-107,178-195`). A universal cache-location or cache-telemetry claim would therefore be false.

- Low — stale current authorities need explicit supersession, as the plan anticipates. ADR 0002 still says the search cache is off by default and working-tree mode stays uncached (`docs/adr/0002-committed-tree-cache-key.md:8-16,120-138`), and `docs/README.md:19,33` still presents it as the accepted cache authority. Current behavior is the opposite for clean interactive worktrees, proven by `internal/sem/search_cache_worktree_test.go:34-68`. Stale implementation comments repeat the old rule at `internal/cli/env.go:46-52` and `internal/sem/search_cache.go:754-756`.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/audit_cli_claims
Payload:
- **High — the planned indexed install is incompatible with the current release artifacts.** Plan lines 23–24, 108–119, 340–341, and 403–407 assume `entire plugin install graph` can install a release. [`scripts/release.sh`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/scripts/release.sh:7) emits hyphenated archives such as `entire-graph-v0.2.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz` and an uppercase `SHA256SUMS` (lines 27–40), while [`entire-plugin.yml`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/entire-plugin.yml:1) provides no `download_url` override. Entire CLI 0.10.0 only considers underscore-style assets such as `entire-graph_0.2.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` and checksum manifests named `checksums.txt` or two lowercase name-prefixed variants ([installer lines 183–223](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.10.0/cmd/entire/cli/plugin_fetch.go#L183-L223)); it otherwise refuses or cannot locate the release ([lines 303–348](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.10.0/cmd/entire/cli/plugin_fetch.go#L303-L348)). The current [v0.2.0 release](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/releases/tag/v0.2.0) also has no assets. This is the format mismatch anticipated by plan lines 448–450 and must be an explicit release prerequisite; adding the index entry alone will not make installation work.

- **High — the publication-time index assumption is currently false.** Plan lines 23–24, 108–117, and 403–404 require the bare index name `graph`. The current official [plugin index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index/blob/0e6cb1be2b620ec62a9ab790b41700de8f030195/index.json#L1-L17) contains only `run` and `upgrade`; the installed CLI reports `No plugins matching "graph" in the index.` Manifest line 1 establishes the plugin’s own name but does not publish an index entry. Because plan lines 443–444 exclude index publication, this must remain a separately owned, publication-blocking prerequisite.

- **Medium — current `init-agents` help contradicts the side effects the plan correctly wants disclosed.** Plan lines 123–126 says the command writes `.entire/graph-agent.md` and marker-delimited pointer blocks in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. [`agents.go`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/agents.go:98) confirms that behavior: the full guide is written at lines 98–105, while lines 107–120 only upsert pointers into the two root files. But [`help.go`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/help.go:68) says it “Writes the operating guide into … AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md” and omits `.entire/graph-agent.md`. That conflicts with plan line 267’s reliance on built-in help and is not covered by the flags-only reconciliation at lines 287–295; the help-prose correction should be tracked as a product prerequisite.

- **Medium — “built-in help remains the exhaustive command surface” is false for accepted aliases.** Plan lines 267 and 291 rely on help while asking that `analyze` be documented as an alias. [`root.go`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/root.go:76) dispatches `analyze`, and lines 696–698 delegate it directly to `diff`; [`help.go`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/help.go:335) deliberately marks it `hidden`, while lines 529–545 omit hidden entries from root help. Root dispatch also accepts `--version`/`-v` and `--help`/`-h` at lines 110–120 without listing those spellings. The plan should call help exhaustive only for canonical visible commands, or require aliases to be exposed/documented separately.

- **Medium — the no-duplicate-import acceptance criterion is unresolved under current `init-agents` behavior.** Plan lines 148–150 acknowledges that a `CLAUDE.md` importing `AGENTS.md` can import the guide twice, but lines 344–346 and 411–413 require the tested activation chain to have no duplicate import, while lines 448–450 exclude an `init-agents` behavior change. [`agents.go`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/agents.go:107) unconditionally writes the same `@.entire/graph-agent.md` pointer into both files. The repository demonstrates the exact two-path layout: [`CLAUDE.md`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/CLAUDE.md:1) imports `AGENTS.md` and directly imports the guide at line 8, while [`AGENTS.md`](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/AGENTS.md:201) contains its own guide pointer. Unless client-side canonical-path deduplication is first proven, the acceptance criterion is not achievable through this documentation-only plan and must be made an explicit blocking assumption or product prerequisite.

The full test suite passes and the branch remains clean. The parallel audits converged on a small set of concrete blockers: the named install cannot yet work from current releases/index metadata, `init-agents` has under-disclosed overwrite/import behavior, and two cache/tree claims need tighter semantics. I’m consolidating those into the final review now.

   280	// RenderExplain prints the block. Unresolved names are listed last and on one line: they are a short

   282	func RenderExplain(response ExplainResponse, maxBytes int) []byte {
   283		if len(response.Symbols) == 0 {
   284			return nil
   285		}
   286		if maxBytes <= 0 {
   287			maxBytes = explainMaxBytes
   288		}
   289		var buffer strings.Builder
   290		buffer.WriteString(ExplainHeader + "\n")
   291		var missing []string
   292		for _, symbol := range response.Symbols {
   293			if !symbol.Resolved {
   294				// Echoed from the build output the caller piped in, which is itself
   295				// produced by a compiler reading repository names.
   296				missing = append(missing, termsafe.Line(symbol.Query))
   297				continue
   298			}
   299			// One declaration per line, so every field is a one-line value: the path
   300			// is a raw Git pathname and the signature is a declaration lifted off a
   301			// line of the scanned tree. Escaped here rather than by wrapping the
   302			// writer, because the byte budget below is measured on these strings and
   303			// has to count what is actually printed.
   304			line := fmt.Sprintf("  %s:%d-%d", termsafe.Line(symbol.FilePath), symbol.StartLine, symbol.EndLine)
   305			if symbol.Kind != "" {
   306				line += " " + termsafe.Line(symbol.Kind)
   307			}
   308			line += " " + termsafe.Line(symbol.Name)
   309			if symbol.Owner != "" {
   310				line += " (in " + termsafe.Line(symbol.Owner) + ")"
   311			}
   312			line += "\n"
   313			if symbol.Signature != "" {
   314				line += "      " + termsafe.Line(strings.Join(strings.Fields(symbol.Signature), " ")) + "\n"
   315			}
   316			if buffer.Len()+len(line) > maxBytes {
   317				break
   318			}
   319			buffer.WriteString(line)
   320		}
   321		if len(missing) > 0 {
   322			line := "  not defined in this repository: " + strings.Join(missing, ", ") + "\n"
   323			if buffer.Len()+len(line) <= maxBytes {
   324				buffer.WriteString(line)
   325			}
   326		}
   327		return []byte(buffer.String())
   328	}

Committed all changes as `d17975a` (`docs: refresh README and reorganize documentation`). The worktree is clean, and `mise run test` passes.

Review findings for [docs/readme-plan.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/readme-plan.md:1):

- **Blocker — indexed installation is not currently publishable.** The official [plugin index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index/blob/main/index.json) lacks `graph`, the current [v0.2.0 release](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/releases/tag/v0.2.0) has no installable plugin archives, and [release.sh](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/scripts/release.sh:27) produces filenames/checksums incompatible with the CLI’s [plugin asset discovery](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.10.0/cmd/entire/cli/plugin_fetch.go#L183-L223). Replace the assumption at [plan:23](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/readme-plan.md:23) with an owned, publication-blocking release/index prerequisite.

- **High — `--head` can mix committed graph data with live working-tree source.** `neighbors` and `impact` load a HEAD snapshot, then annotate results from disk ([neighbors.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/neighbors.go:153), [impact.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/impact.go:140)); `def` has similar live-body behavior, and `explain --head` still prints “from the working tree” ([explain.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/explain.go:332)). This needs an explicit product prerequisite before documenting exact tree semantics.

- **High — the no-duplicate-import acceptance criterion is presently unattainable.** `init-agents` always writes pointers to both files, while this repository’s [CLAUDE.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/CLAUDE.md:1) imports `AGENTS.md` and the guide directly; [AGENTS.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/AGENTS.md:201) imports it again. The plan acknowledges this at [line 148](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/readme-plan.md:148) but requires no duplicate import at [line 411](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/readme-plan.md:411). Define a supported manual layout, relax the criterion, or make import-aware behavior a product prerequisite.

- **Medium — activation side effects are under-disclosed.** `.entire/graph-agent.md` is overwritten wholesale on every run ([agents.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/agents.go:98)); marker idempotence only holds for one intact block. The README plan should disclose overwrite behavior and document malformed/duplicate-marker recovery.

- **Medium — “any dirty graph-relevant path disables reuse” is inaccurate.** Dirty indexable files and resolver manifests bypass caching ([search_cache.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/search_cache.go:145)), but `.graphignore` changes instead select a content-keyed cache entry ([search_cache.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/sem/search_cache.go:831)). Tighten the wording at [plan:203](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/readme-plan.md:203).

- **Medium — `index` prewarming is profile/options-specific.** `index` defaults to `full` ([index.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/index.go:181)), while `search` defaults to `fast` ([search.go](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/internal/cli/search.go:1718). Therefore a default `index` run does not warm a bare `search --head`; the plan should specify matching profile and graph-shaping options.

- **Medium — cache ADR supersession needs explicit mechanics.** ADR 0002 remains accepted and says working-tree mode is uncached ([ADR 0002](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/adr/0002-committed-tree-cache-key.md:134)), while the docs index still names it authoritative. The plan should name the replacement ADR, mark ADR 0002 superseded with a forward link, and update [docs/README.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/README.md:33).

No review edits were made, and nothing was pushed.

# GitHub Publish Changes

## Overview

Use this skill only when the user explicitly wants the full publish flow from the local checkout: branch setup if needed, staging, commit, push, and opening a pull request.

This workflow is hybrid:

- Use local `git` for branch creation, staging, commit, and push.
- Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for pull request creation after the branch is on the remote.
- Use `gh` as a fallback for current-branch PR discovery, auth checks, or PR creation when the connector path cannot infer the repository or head branch cleanly.

## Prerequisites

- Require GitHub CLI `gh`. Check `gh --version`. If missing, ask the user to install `gh` and stop.
- Require authenticated `gh` session. Run `gh auth status`. If not authenticated, ask the user to run `gh auth login` (and re-run `gh auth status`) before continuing.
- Require a local git repository with a clean understanding of which changes belong in the PR.

## Naming conventions

- Branch: `agent/{description}` when starting from main/master/default.
- Commit: `{description}` (terse).
- PR title: `{description}` summarizing the full diff.

## Workflow

1. Confirm intended scope.
   - Run `git status -sb` and inspect the diff before staging.
   - If the working tree contains unrelated changes, do not default to `git add -A`. Ask the user which files belong in the PR.
2. Determine the branch strategy.
   - If on `main`, `master`, or another default branch, create `agent/{description}`.
   - Otherwise stay on the current branch.
3. Stage only the intended changes.
   - Prefer explicit file paths when the worktree is mixed.
   - Use `git add -A` only when the user has confirmed the whole worktree belongs in scope.
4. Commit tersely with the confirmed description.
5. Run the most relevant checks available if they have not already been run.
   - If checks fail due to missing dependencies or tools, install what is needed and rerun once.
6. Push with tracking: `git push -u origin $(git branch --show-current)`.
7. Open a draft PR.
   - Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for PR creation after the push succeeds.
   - Derive `repository_full_name` from the remote, for example by normalizing `git remote get-url origin` or by using `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`.
   - Derive `head_branch` from `git branch --show-current`.
   - Derive `base_branch` from the user request when specified; otherwise use the remote default branch, for example via `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`.
   - If the branch is being pushed from a fork or the PR target differs from the remote that was just pushed, prefer `gh pr create` fallback because the connector PR creation flow expects one repository target and may not encode cross-repo head semantics cleanly.
   - If connector-based PR creation cannot infer the repository or branch cleanly, fall back to `gh pr create --draft --fill --head $(git branch --show-current)`.
   - Write the PR body to a temp file with real newlines when using CLI fallback so the markdown renders cleanly.
8. Summarize the result with branch name, commit, PR target, validation, and anything the user still needs to confirm.

## Write Safety

- Never stage unrelated user changes silently.
- Never push without confirming scope when the worktree is mixed.
- Default to a draft PR unless the user explicitly asks for a ready-for-review PR.
- If the repository does not appear to be connected to an accessible GitHub remote, stop and explain the blocker before making assumptions.

## PR Body Expectations

The PR description should use real Markdown prose and cover:

- what changed
- why it changed
- the user or developer impact
- the root cause when the PR is a fix
- the checks used to validate it

    18			printf 'invalid target %s; expected GOOS/GOARCH\n' "$1" >&2
    19			return 1
    20		fi
    21

    25		esac
    26	
    27		work="$out_dir/entire-graph-$version-$goos-$goarch"
    28		archive="$out_dir/entire-graph-$version-$goos-$goarch.tar.gz"
    29		rm -rf "$work"
    30		mkdir -p "$work"
    31	
    32		printf 'building %s/%s\n' "$goos" "$goarch" >&2
    33		GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" CGO_ENABLED="${CGO_ENABLED:-1}" \
    34			go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=$version" \
    35			-o "$work/$bin" ./cmd/entire-graph
    36	
    37		cp README.md LICENSE entire-plugin.yml "$work/"
    38		tar -C "$out_dir" -czf "$archive" "entire-graph-$version-$goos-$goarch"
    39		rm -rf "$work"
    40		shasum -a 256 "$archive" >> "$out_dir/SHA256SUMS"
    41		sign_artifact "$archive"
    42	}
    43	
    44	sign_artifact() {
    45		artifact=$1
    46		if [ -n "${COSIGN_KEY:-}" ] && command -v cosign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    47			cosign sign-blob --yes --key "$COSIGN_KEY" --output-signature "$artifact.sig" "$artifact"
    48			return
    49		fi
    50		if [ -n "${GPG_SIGNING_KEY:-}" ] && command -v gpg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    51			gpg --batch --yes --armor --detach-sign --local-user "$GPG_SIGNING_KEY" --output "$artifact.asc" "$artifact"
    52		fi
    53	}
    54	
    55	for target in $targets; do
    56		build_target "$target"
    57	done
    58	
    59	printf 'wrote %s\n' "$out_dir" >&2

1	# Entire Plugin Index
     2	
     3	The plugin catalog for the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli). `entire plugin search`, `install <name>`, `info`, and `browse` resolve bare plugin names through this repository.
     4	
     5	```sh
     6	entire plugin search            # browse the catalog
     7	entire plugin install upgrade   # install by name
     8	entire plugin index update      # force a refresh
     9	```
    10	
    11	## How it works
    12	
    13	There is no hosted service. The CLI shallow-clones this repository into its user cache and re-pulls it on a TTL (default 24 hours) — any git server can host an index, and the CLI keeps working offline from its cached copy. The catalog is the single `index.json` file at the repository root.
    14	
    15	Plugins themselves are standalone executables named `entire-<name>`. Installing one resolves the newest semver tag of its repository over the git protocol (`git ls-remote`), downloads the platform's release asset over HTTPS, verifies it against the release's `checksums.txt`, and places it in the CLI's managed plugin directory. See the [external commands documentation](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-commands.md) for the full contract.
    16	
    17	## index.json schema (version 1)
    18	
    19	```json
    20	{
    21	  "version": 1,
    22	  "plugins": [
    23	    {
    24	      "name": "upgrade",
    25	      "repo_url": "https://github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade",
    26	      "description": "Upgrade the system-installed Entire binary",
    27	      "official": true,
    28	      "platforms": ["darwin", "linux", "windows"]
    29	    }
    30	  ]
    31	}
    32	```
    33	
    34	| Field | Required | Meaning |
    35	|---|---|---|
    36	| `name` | yes | Bare plugin name (`upgrade` for `entire-upgrade`). Must be a valid dispatcher name: no path separators, no leading `-`, and the `agent-` prefix is reserved for the external agent protocol. |
    37	| `repo_url` | yes | Full `https://` git URL of the plugin repository. Any git host works — GitHub, GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, self-hosted. |
    38	| `description` | no | One line, shown by `search`, `info`, and `browse`. |
    39	| `official` | no | Marks Entire-maintained plugins. Defaults to `false`. |
    40	| `platforms` | no | Supported GOOS values when the plugin doesn't ship the full matrix. Empty means all. |
    41	
    42	Entries with invalid names or missing repo URLs are filtered by the CLI on load, not fatal — but don't rely on that.
    43	
    44	## Adding a plugin
    45	
    46	1. **Name and host your repository.** Convention: the repository basename is `entire-<name>`. Releases must be downloadable without authentication (public repository).
    47	2. **Publish releases with conventional assets.** Tag with semver (`v0.1.0`) and attach per-platform assets named `entire-<name>_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` (`.zip` on Windows) containing the `entire-<name>` binary, plus a `checksums.txt` (sha256sum format). goreleaser's defaults produce exactly this shape — see [entire-upgrade's `.goreleaser.yaml`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade/blob/main/.goreleaser.yaml) for a working template. Hosts with non-standard release URLs can declare a `download_url` template in `entire-plugin.yml` instead.
    48	3. **Optionally commit `entire-plugin.yml`** at the repository root:
    49	
    50	   ```yaml
    51	   name: myplugin
    52	   description: One-line description
    53	   requires:                # other plugins this one needs (optional)
    54	     - name: sem
    55	       repo_url: https://github.com/entireio/entire-sem
    56	       min_version: v0.2.0  # minimum only; no range syntax
    57	   ```
    58	
    59	4. **Open a pull request** adding your entry to `index.json`. Keep the list sorted by name.
    60	
    61	Before submitting, verify the end-to-end flow works against your repository directly:
    62	
    63	```sh
    64	entire plugin install https://github.com/you/entire-myplugin --yes
    65	entire myplugin
    66	entire plugin remove myplugin
    67	```
    68	
    69	## Private and corporate catalogs
    70	
    71	Organizations can host their own index (any git repository with an `index.json`) and point the CLI at it. Precedence, highest first:
    72	
    73	1. `--index <url>` flag on the plugin subcommands
    74	2. `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` environment variable
    75	3. `plugins.index_url` in `.entire/settings.local.json` / `.entire/settings.json` — commit it to a repository to point every contributor at an internal catalog
    76	4. This repository (the built-in default)
    77	
    78	`plugins.index_ttl_hours` tunes refresh frequency (default 24).
